card.name: Linking words before a niacin-type or ni- word
card.fires_on: Commas, small linking words such as of, in, to, is, and the word Twitter, where the next word may be a ni-starting term. It shows up in lists of symptoms, drugs or side effects, and in passages about niacin (nicotinic acid).

modes.label: Commas in lists
modes.description: A comma after an item in a list of drugs or symptoms, just before the next item.
modes.example: It can cause flushing of the skin<<,>> nausea, diarrhea, and liver damage.

modes.label: Small linking words
modes.description: A short word like of, in, to or is that sits right before a noun phrase.
modes.example: Flushing is an increase in blood passing through the veins<< in>> the skin, due to the dilation of

modes.label: Social media name
modes.description: The word Twitter right after a hashtag.

card.writes: It nudges the next word toward ni- starts such as Ni, Nick and nicotinic-type names, and away from broken characters.
card.plain: It fires on commas and small joining words in lists, mostly near niacin text, where a word starting with ni might come next.
